intro: Tuition work in Kohima is organised into four zones. North Kohima & Kohima Village runs from the old settlement on the north-eastern heights through Kitsübozou, Naga Bazaar, Peraciezie and Bayavü Hill; Main Town & Midland holds Daklane, New Market, Midland and Officers' Hill; Chandmari & PR Hill covers Upper and Lower Chandmari and PR Hill; and Lerie & Agri Farm takes in Lerie, Agri Farm and Merhülietsa on the southern and south-western edge. This is a hill city with no rail line of its own, where buses and taxis carry most people. Many homes sit above or below the road on stepped paths, so the useful skill is reading a ward, its upper or lower part and a landmark, then knowing where a taxi or two-wheeler can stop.

Most of the board work you will meet is for the Nagaland Board of School Education, whose HSLC paper closes Class 10 and whose HSSLC paper closes Class 12 across three streams, or for CBSE. Some schools follow CISCE's ICSE and ISC, and IB or Cambridge IGCSE learners mostly find a specialist online. The NBSE website publishes the syllabus, blueprints for the HSLC and HSSLC papers, lists of prescribed textbooks, a question bank with past question papers, the academic calendar and exam routines, and the board's office is at Upper Bayavü Hill. Teach from those documents rather than forwarded copies, and state your boards, classes and streams clearly on your profile.

Home and online work fit together across Kohima's year. Rain is heaviest from June to September, when families often keep one weekly session online, and board-year students tend to want extra sessions from the winter onwards. When a family in Midland, for example, sends a request, NXTutors shortlists two or three tutors, starting with those in that ward, then the Main Town & Midland zone, then the rest of Kohima, then online, and the family sees each fee before a free first demo; changing tutor later costs the family nothing. Because online learners may live in any Indian city, your teaching week need not stop at the wards you can reach in person.

zone_notes.North Kohima & Kohima Village: Homes here climb the north-eastern slopes, from Kohima Village and Kitsübozou down through Naga Bazaar to Peraciezie and Bayavü Hill, so ask each family for the ward, its upper or lower part, a landmark and the nearest point a taxi can reach. If you live in the southern wards, avoid start times just after offices close, when the central stretch is busiest. The board office at Upper Bayavü Hill brings extra visitors on working days.
zone_notes.Main Town & Midland: Daklane and New Market are the easiest wards to reach from anywhere and the hardest to time: roads are busiest when offices open and close, and parking near New Market can be tight. In Midland, check whether the home is in Upper, Middle or Lower Midland. At Officers' Hill, also called Thegabakha, the hill roads are narrow, so ask the family where to leave a two-wheeler before the first visit.
zone_notes.Chandmari & PR Hill: Upper and Lower Chandmari are separate wards with similar names, so confirm which one before a first visit; PR Hill's ward also covers Lower PR Hill. Families often give the Capital Cultural Centre at PR Hill or a large place of worship in Lower Chandmari as landmarks. Weekday roads towards the centre fill at office hours, so late-afternoon or evening slots suit tutors travelling in from Midland or Officers' Hill.
zone_notes.Lerie & Agri Farm: This southern and south-western edge holds Lerie with New Ministers' Hill and New Reserve, Agri Farm with Upper Agri, Electrical and Forest, and Merhülietsa with Lower Agri. Upper and Lower Agri sit in different wards, so check every address twice. Tutors crossing from the northern wards usually take later evening or weekend slots, while those living in PR Hill or the Chandmari wards can come straight after school.

boards: In Kohima a tutor may prepare one student for the NBSE's HSLC in Class 10, another for the HSSLC in Class 12, and a third for CBSE from the NCERT books. ICSE and ISC appear where a school is affiliated to CISCE, and IB or Cambridge IGCSE requests are fewer and mostly online. Each board keeps its own documents: NBSE posts syllabus, blueprints, textbook lists, its question bank and exam routines on nbsenl.edu.in, CBSE on its academic portal, CISCE on cisce.org. Name your boards, classes and streams on the profile.

board_cards.name: Nagaland Board of School Education (NBSE)
board_cards.note: NBSE conducts the HSLC examination for Class 10 and the HSSLC examination for Class 12 in arts, science and commerce streams. Its website publishes the syllabus, blueprints for both papers, lists of prescribed textbooks and a question bank with past papers. Plan lessons around those textbooks and blueprints, and take exam routines from the board itself rather than from shared screenshots.

board_cards.name: CBSE
board_cards.note: CBSE students in Kohima live alongside NBSE ones, sometimes in the same ward. Build lessons on the NCERT textbooks, use the board's own sample papers and marking schemes for practice, and get students writing complete, stepped answers. Because JEE and NEET draw on the same NCERT base, thorough chapter work in Classes 11 and 12 serves both goals.

board_cards.name: CISCE (ICSE and ISC)
board_cards.note: Some Kohima schools prepare students for CISCE's ICSE at Class 10 and ISC at Class 12. Both mean lengthy written answers over a wide syllabus, set texts in English, and internal assessment in many subjects. Finishing the syllabus with time to spare is the hard part, so build two or three revision passes and regular timed answers. CISCE publishes its regulations and specimen papers online.

women.intro: Women tutors are welcome on NXTutors in Kohima, teaching at home, online or both. The wards you pick and the hours you open decide which requests reach you: someone in Midland could stay with the central wards and the Chandmari side, someone in Kitsübozou with the northern slopes, and anyone else can learn with you online. Because many homes are reached by stepped paths, it is reasonable to ask the family to meet you at the road on a first visit. All tutors who sign up go through one ID check, we ask a parent to be at home for the demo, and one safeguarding policy applies to both sides. Treat these as working controls, not promises about people.
points: Switch between home, online or both from your profile at any time.
Add only wards you are glad to travel to; leaving out long cross-town evening trips is fine.
Open only the hours that work for you, and close late slots in the June to September rains if you wish.
Every new family starts with a free demo, and we ask a parent to be at home for it.
Settle fee, timing and messages with the parent rather than the child.
With young students, work in a common room with an adult in the house; on video, both cameras stay on.
Registration means a one-time code to your phone or email plus a government photo ID that our team checks.
Feel uneasy at any point? End the session, tell NXTutors with the word Safeguarding, and in an emergency dial 112 first.

story: Sign up from your phone. A one-time code confirms your number or email; then fill in subjects, classes, boards like NBSE, CBSE or ICSE, and the Kohima wards you can reach every week.
Add a government photo ID next. Our team looks at it before any family sees you, and one ID can be linked to only one tutor account. This proves identity; it is not a police or background check.
With the review complete, families can open your profile: boards, the wards you cover between Kohima Village and Lerie, whether you teach at home, online or both, and your own hourly fee.
Picture a parent in Naga Bazaar or PR Hill asking for help. NXTutors draws up two or three tutors, looking first at that ward, next its zone, then all of Kohima, and lastly online.
Before booking, the parent sees what you charge. Lesson one is a free demo in their home, and we ask a parent to be at home, so you meet the student and learn the route and timing.
From then on, teach the homes within reach, online learners anywhere in India, or both, perhaps visiting through the term and moving online on the wettest days between June and September.
faqs: How do tuition requests in Kohima reach tutors?

A parent fills in the class, board, subjects, ward and landmark, and chooses home, online or a mix. NXTutors then shortlists two or three tutors, checking the same ward first, then its zone, then the wider city, then online. Whether your name comes up depends on the wards and boards you have listed.
Can I teach students outside Nagaland online while living in Kohima?

Yes. Online lessons reach learners across India, so you can take home students near your own ward and teach others online. Home requests are matched to nearby tutors first; an online request can come to you from a family in any state.
Which Kohima wards should I list on my profile?

Only those you can reach at the agreed hour every week. A tutor in Upper Chandmari might list Lower Chandmari, PR Hill and Midland, while one in Naga Bazaar might keep to Daklane, Kitsübozou and Peraciezie. Think about the June to September rains too: a short, honest list is easier to keep.
What happens in the ID check for Kohima tutors?

Two steps: a one-time code sent to your phone or email, and a government photo ID that our team looks at before your profile is marked Verified. It establishes who you are and nothing more; police records and background are not checked. Read /how-we-verify-tutors for the full process.
Do I pay to join NXTutors as a tutor?

Yes. Tutor plans are paid; /pricing lists them and the features in each. Your hourly rate is a different matter: you decide it, and parents see it before the free first demo. Since a family may change tutor later without paying anything, regular, well-prepared lessons are what keep a student with you.
Can a woman tutor in Kohima limit home visits to wards near her own?

Yes. Home requests follow the wards you list, so a tutor might accept visits only in Midland or Kitsübozou and take all other students online. Because we ask a parent to be at home for the free demo, you see the household first and agree a timetable only if it suits you.
Which boards can I teach in Kohima?

Students here follow the Nagaland Board of School Education or CBSE, and some schools follow CISCE's ICSE and ISC; IB and Cambridge IGCSE learners usually study online. List your boards, classes and streams, and for NBSE students work from the prescribed textbooks and the blueprints and question bank on the board's website.
Can one Kohima student have both home and online lessons with me?

Yes. Turn on both modes and settle the split with the parent once the demo is done. One workable pattern is home visits during term with one session shifted online in the wettest weeks of June to September, which keeps the routine intact when travel is slow.
